msg: The eighth section of Paper 101 carefully distinguishes belief from faith. As the terms are used here, belief is the intellectual assent that accepts a teaching as fact, while faith is the living trust that moves the whole of life. The passage says that belief has attained the level of faith when it motivates life and shapes the mode of living. The acceptance of a teaching as true is not faith; that is mere belief. Neither is certainty nor conviction faith.

This distinction calls for honest self-examination. I say I believe that God is love. But does that belief actually govern my day? When worries crowd in, when someone has hurt me, when I must accept a loss, is that belief guiding my choices? In the words of the passage, a state of mind attains to faith levels only when it actually dominates the mode of living. Faith is not assent in the head but movement in the life.

The passage also makes clear the object of faith. One believes truth, admires beauty, and reverences goodness, but does not worship them; such an attitude of saving faith is centered on God alone, who is all of these personified and infinitely more. Ideals such as truth and goodness are precious, but our final trust and worship must be directed to the living, personal God who is the source of those ideals.

The following paragraph sets two things in contrast. Belief is always limiting and binding; faith is expanding and releasing. Belief fixates, faith liberates. Beliefs may become group possessions, but faith must be personal; theologic beliefs can be suggested to a group, but faith can rise up only in the heart of the individual religionist. And so the passage sums up faith as God-knowing and man-serving. Faith is more than the association of noble beliefs, more than an exalted system of philosophy; it is a living experience.

To say that belief binds is not to say that belief is bad. Sound belief provides a framework in which faith can grow. The trouble comes when we stop at belief and think that guarding it is the whole of religion. Then we judge others from inside the fence of our own doctrines and shut the door on new truth. Faith carries us beyond that fence, ever onward toward God, and opens our hearts toward people. As Paper 102 says, faith is the living power that triumphs over doubt (see Paper 102, section 6).

Today, choose one of the things you say you believe and actually live it. If you believe God cares for you, entrust one worry to him today; if you believe all people are brothers, approach one person today with a brother’s heart. When belief becomes action, action becomes habit, and habit becomes a way of living, our belief grows into a liberating faith. Belief is the door to faith, and faith is the road we walk with the Father once we pass through that door. Let us not stand before the door admiring its shape; let us open it today and take one step through. That one step will set us free from what has bound us.
d198.pr: Choose one truth you say you believe, and live it today through one concrete action.

msg: Paper 102 deals with the foundations of religious faith. It opens with the despairing outlook of the unbelieving materialist, for whom man is merely an accidental product of evolution whose hopes and dreams will finally vanish in a cold universe (see Paper 102, introduction). But it immediately declares that this is not man’s destiny. Today’s passage points to an inner evidence that man is by no means an accidental being: the holy hunger that continually rises within us.

The passage says that the indwelling Thought Adjuster unfailingly arouses in man’s soul a true and searching hunger for perfection. The Adjuster also awakens a far-reaching curiosity which can be adequately satisfied only by communion with God, the divine source of that Adjuster. This is why, however much we possess and achieve, we still feel deep in our hearts that something is missing. That hunger is not a defect; it is a sign that God is within us.

The passage goes on to say that the hungry soul of man refuses to be satisfied with anything less than the personal realization of the living God. People try hard to fill this hunger with other things: success, wealth, pleasure, recognition, a busy schedule. But these only help us forget the hunger for a while; they cannot satisfy it. For what the soul seeks is not some object or achievement but a living person, a meeting with the Father who knows and loves us.

The last sentence of the passage is also worth taking deeply to heart: whatever more God may be than a high and perfect moral personality, he cannot, in our hungry and finite concept, be anything less. God is far greater than anything we can imagine, but at the very least he is personal, good, and loving. The soul’s hunger cannot be satisfied by an impersonal force or a vague principle, because love passes only between person and person.

This teaching helps us see our dissatisfaction and longing in a new light. When life feels empty, when an emptiness sweeps over us that nothing seems to fill, do not try to cover it with more possessions or busier activity. It may be the voice of the Adjuster calling us to the Father. When we accept that longing honestly and bring it to God in prayer and worship, our hunger is gradually transformed into the joy of communion. Of course, longing never fully ends in this world, for the hunger for perfection is the very power that draws us forward all along the eternal path of ascension.

Today, let us quietly look into the hunger within us. With what are we trying to fill that empty place? Invite God into it. Even a short prayer will do. When we confess in our hearts, “Father, what I am truly seeking is you,” our souls remember again where they came from and where they must go. That remembering becomes the foundation of faith. Only those who know their hunger go looking for bread. So do not be ashamed of the hunger of your heart; receive it as the tender beckoning of the Adjuster drawing you to the Father. Day after day of following that beckoning becomes the road of eternal communion.
d199.pr: When your heart feels empty today, pause before filling it with something else, and tell God what is in your heart.

msg: The sixth section of Paper 102 deals with the certainty of religious faith. As science advances and philosophy clears away old fears, many people feel that the place left for faith is steadily shrinking. But this paper says that, on the contrary, true faith can stand more firmly than ever. Today’s passage explains why: belief may not be able to resist doubt and withstand fear, but faith is always triumphant over doubting, for faith is both positive and living.

Here the distinction between belief and faith appears again. A belief accepted only in the head can waver before a strong counterargument, for what has been built by logic can collapse before stronger logic. But faith comes from a living relationship with God. Just as trust in someone we love does not vanish because of a single argument, faith that knows God by experience does not crumble before the questions of doubt. Rather, it grows deeper by passing through doubt.

The passage explains this principle of victory through four contrasts: the positive always has the advantage over the negative, truth over error, experience over theory, spiritual realities over the isolated facts of time and space. Doubt is by nature negative; it is a power that tears down rather than builds. Faith, on the other hand, moves toward something, builds something, and is filled with living experience. As darkness retreats when light comes in, doubt loses its power before living faith.

Where, then, is the evidence of such spiritual certainty? The passage says it consists in the social fruits of the spirit which such believers, faithers, yield as a result of this genuine spiritual experience. And it quotes the words of Jesus: “⟦Q 102:6.7⟧If you love your fellows as I have loved you, then shall all men know that you are my disciples.⟦/Q⟧” The most convincing evidence of faith is not argument but a loving life. The last section of Paper 102 likewise says that the highest evidence of religion lies in the fact of human experience, in transformed lives (see Paper 102, section 8).

This teaching is a great comfort to those troubled by doubt. Having doubts does not mean having no faith. Doubt comes naturally to anyone who thinks. What matters is not spending our time arguing with doubt but continuing to walk the positive path of faith. When we do not stop praying, loving, and serving, doubt has somehow fallen behind us. Faith overcomes doubt not so much by logic as by life.

Today, when doubt raises its head in your heart, rather than wrestling with it, choose one act of love. In the moment of helping, comforting, or forgiving someone, we experience anew that God is living. And the fruit of that love becomes the clearest testimony that faith is true, not only to ourselves but to those who are watching us. It is all right if some doubt remains. Whoever walks the path of love, even while still holding doubts, is already living by faith. Along that path doubts are resolved one by one, and the assurance of knowing God quietly grows. In the end, faith becomes certain to the degree that it is lived.
d200.pr: When doubt or anxiety comes, rather than arguing with it, carry out one act of love for someone.

d201.t: The Father Who Sees Our Motives
msg: Paper 103 deals with the reality of religious experience, and its fourth section speaks of spiritual communion with God. Whenever primitive peoples felt that their fellowship with God had been broken, they tried to restore the relationship by offering sacrifices and performing rites of atonement (see Paper 103, section 4). Such rites arose mostly from fear and guilt. Today’s passage shows how Jesus lifted this ancient religious burden from us.

The passage says that Jesus swept away all of the ceremonials of sacrifice and atonement. He destroyed the basis of all this fictitious guilt and sense of isolation in the universe by declaring that man is a child of God. The creature-Creator relationship was placed on a child-parent basis, and God becomes a loving Father to his mortal sons and daughters. And all ceremonials not a legitimate part of such an intimate family relationship are forever abrogated.

This is a truly revolutionary declaration. Just as a child does not offer sacrifices to win a father’s love, we need not offer anything to win God’s love. We are already beloved children. Worship and prayer are not ways of buying or buying back our relationship with the Father, but ways of enjoying and expressing a relationship already given. As Paper 98 says, the Creator Son did not come to appease an angry God but to reveal the Father’s love (see Paper 98, section 7).

The following paragraph explains how this relationship works. God the Father deals with man his child on the basis, not of actual virtue or worthiness, but in recognition of the child’s motivation, the creature purpose and intent. The relationship is one of parent-child association and is actuated by divine love. We are still imperfect; we make many mistakes and do not do as well as we would like. But God looks not at the score of our results but at the direction of our hearts. If we sincerely desire the good and are moved to do the Father’s will, he treasures that motive.

This teaching gives deep freedom to those who struggle with perfectionism and guilt. We are not students holding out a report card before God and waiting for judgment. We are children standing before a Father who warmly watches as his little one falls and gets up again. Yet this truth must not become an excuse for irresponsibility. If our motives are sincere, we will naturally strive to do better. Sincere motives always give birth to growth.

Today, let us examine the motives behind our actions. What do we do to look good to others, to avoid punishment, or to gain a reward, and what do we do out of love for the Father and care for our brothers? And if we have made a mistake today, let us not hide it or berate ourselves, but bring it honestly to the Father. He is one who looks first at the sincere heart before our clumsy results. In place of the old religion of offering sacrifices, Jesus gave us the intimate conversation of a child with the Father. Our part is to carry on that conversation every day. Without any grand ritual, with nothing but a sincere heart, we can stand before the Father at any time. That is the new and living way Jesus opened for us.
d201.pr: Choose one thing you did today, examine its motive honestly, and offer a pure motive to the Father afresh.

msg: The fifth section of Paper 103 deals with the origin of ideals. From early on, man experiences conflict between the urge to serve himself and the urge to serve others, and in that conflict he learns moral choice. The paragraph just before says that in the spiritual realm man truly has free will (see Paper 103, section 5). Today’s passage stresses how essential that freedom is to spiritual growth: man is not saved or ennobled by pressure.

The passage says that spirit growth springs from within the evolving soul. Pressure may deform the personality, but it never stimulates growth. Even educational pressure is only negatively helpful in that it may aid in the prevention of disastrous experiences. And so spiritual growth is greatest where all external pressures are at a minimum. Quoting the words “⟦Q 103:5.11⟧Where the spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom,⟦/Q⟧” the passage says that man develops best when the pressures of home, community, church, and state are least.

This teaching is closely tied to the way God deals with us. The Universal Father does not drag us along by force. The Thought Adjuster dwells within us yet never goes against our will, and the angels too do not limit man’s prerogative of choice (see Paper 113, section 5). What God desires is not servants who obey under compulsion but children who freely choose to love. Goodness that is forced is not true goodness, and commandments kept out of fear cannot make the soul grow.

But the passage does not lose its balance. It adds plainly that this must not be construed as meaning that there is no place in a progressive society for home, social institutions, church, and state. These institutions protect and nurture people and provide an order for living together. Their role, however, should not be to force people into a mold but to provide good soil in which each person can grow freely. As Paper 100 says, we cannot cause growth, but we can supply favorable conditions for it.

This teaching puts an important question to all who live as parents, teachers, and leaders: Am I trying to manufacture the faith and character of my children or my colleagues by force? Paper 100 counsels that we give the growing child the opportunity to develop his own religious experience and not force adult experience upon him. Setting an example, waiting in love, and leaving room for others to choose for themselves is the most powerful influence. The same is true of how we treat ourselves. It is not self-reproach and whipping ourselves on but a spontaneous love of truth that makes the soul grow.

Today, let us find one pressure we are putting on someone and lay it down. Choose example instead of nagging, invitation instead of compulsion, patience instead of hurry. And allow yourself the same freedom. Where the spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom, and in that freedom our souls grow of their own accord toward God. Freedom is not license but the condition that makes love possible. Only when people are not coerced can they choose the good from the heart, and only the good they choose for themselves becomes a value that endures forever in the soul. This is precisely why God has given us freedom.
d202.pr: Lay down one pressure you have been putting on a family member or colleague today, and invite them instead by a warm example.

d203.t: The Harmony of Love and Law
msg: Paper 104 traces how the concept of the Trinity has grown through human history. Adam and Eve, Melchizedek, and Jesus taught this truth in turn, and many peoples strove in their own ways to lay hold of it. Today’s passage explains why the rather difficult concept of the Trinity is of real help to our life of faith: through the recognition of the Trinity concept the mind of man can hope to grasp something of the interrelationship of love and law in the time-space creations.

The passage honestly names a confusion that believers often experience. Through spiritual faith man gains insight into the love of God, but soon discovers that this spiritual faith has no influence on the ordained laws of the material universe. However earnestly we pray, gravity still acts, illness runs its natural course, and accidents happen according to the law of cause and effect. For those who believe in a God of love, this sometimes becomes a great question: If God really loves me, why does this happen?

The passage gives us a clue to this question. Irrespective of the firmness of man’s belief in God as his Paradise Father, expanding cosmic horizons demand that he also give recognition to the reality of Paradise Deity as universal law. They demand that he recognize the Trinity sovereignty extending outward from Paradise and overshadowing even the evolving local universes of the Creator Sons and Creative Daughters. The Father’s love and the law of the universe do not come from two different gods; they come together from the indivisible union of the three eternal persons, the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit.

This truth shows us the way of mature faith. Law is not the opposite of love. The orderly laws of the universe are in fact also an expression of love on which every creature can rely and depend. If God changed the laws of nature at will according to each person’s wishes, the universe would fall into chaos, and no one could foresee the future or live responsibly. The very next paragraph tells us that Jesus taught that justice is never a personal act but always a group function (see Paper 104, section 2). Love is personal, but law and justice preserve the order of the whole universe.

So we should not think of prayer as a spell that overturns the laws of nature. Prayer changes not so much the laws as ourselves, who live within those laws. It gives us courage in illness, meaning in loss, and strength to make wise choices in difficult circumstances. And we can respect the laws of nature, take care of our bodies, accept outcomes humbly, and trust through it all that the Father’s love is with us. A faith that embraces both love and law is not easily disappointed.

Today, call to mind one thing you cannot change. Do not take it as God’s indifference or punishment, but accept it as an event in a universe ruled by love and law together. Then look for the loving choice you can make within it. When we do this, we come to understand the truth of the Trinity not only with our heads but with our lives. The one who believes in love while respecting law, and who follows law without losing love, is the one who best knows the God of the Trinity.
d203.pr: Think of one thing you cannot change, and find and carry out one loving choice you can make within it.

d204.t: A Universe of Love and Order
msg: The fourth section of Paper 104 describes the seven triunities. The first triunity is the personal and purposive union of love, mercy, and ministry; the second triunity is the triunity of power and pattern, which governs all the patterns of the universe, from the tiniest ultimatonic particles to the mighty stars and galaxies. Such teaching may sound distant and abstract to us. But today’s passage links this deep cosmological truth to our religious experience.

The passage first says that in religious experience creatures make contact with the God who is love. This is the center of faith. The one we meet when we pray and worship is not a cold principle or an impersonal force but the Father who loves us as his children. But the passage immediately strikes a balance: such spiritual insight must never eclipse the intelligent recognition of the universe fact of the pattern which is Paradise. However precious the experience of love may be, it must never become a reason to disregard the order and structure of the universe.

The passage then tells how the Paradise personalities lead creatures. They enlist the freewill adoration of all creatures by the compelling power of divine love. It is not coercion or threat but the persuasion of love. And they lead all spirit-born personalities into the supernal delights of the unending service of the finaliter sons of God. Our eternal future is the joy of unending service, and the power that draws us along that road is love.

Meanwhile, the passage says, the second triunity is the architect of the space stage whereon these transactions unfold; it determines the patterns of cosmic configuration. If love is the theme of the story, pattern is the stage on which the story unfolds. Without an orderly stage, the story of love could not unfold at all. Because galaxies turn by fixed laws, atoms follow set structures, and life evolves in an orderly way, personalities can love one another, grow, and find their way to the Father. The exquisite order of the universe itself reveals the wisdom of the loving God.

This teaching also brings balance to our life of faith. Some emphasize only warm feeling and the experience of love and neglect the role of order, principle, and intellect. Others are so occupied with structures and rules that they lose living love. In God, love and pattern are not in conflict. So it should be in our lives as well. The heart should be warm while the mind stays clear; love should be deep while the order of life stays well kept. Love blossoms best not in chaos but in beautiful order.

Today, look up at the sky or gaze at a single small flower and feel the order of the universe. And remember that the One who designed that order is the very Father who loves you. If there is a place in your life where love is scattered without order, or where there is only order and love has dried up, choose one and set it right. When we embrace love and order together, we come to resemble the pattern of Paradise a little more. An orderly universe is the home where God’s love dwells, and within that home we freely love, serve, and grow. Love is the power that moves us, and order is the vessel that keeps that power from scattering in vain.
d204.pr: Observe one example of the order of nature, meditate on the love of the Father who designed it, and give thanks.

msg: Paper 105, which deals with Deity and reality, is one of the most philosophical and difficult papers in The Urantia Book. It explores how the finite mind can understand the I AM, the Infinite who is the source of all reality. Even to the higher orders of universe intelligences, the paper says, infinity is only partially comprehensible. Amid such deep discussion, today’s passage shines out a warm truth like a lamp lit in the darkness.

The passage begins with an honest admission: infinity is indeed remote from the experience level of mortal comprehension. Our minds are made to think in terms of beginnings and endings, large and small, here and there, so we cannot fully grasp an infinity without limits. Yet the passage tells us not to lose heart. Even in this age on Urantia our concepts of infinity are growing, and they will continue to grow throughout our endless careers stretching onward into future eternity.

These words hold great hope. Our understanding of God does not have to be complete now. The God we know today will be known more greatly and deeply tomorrow, and that understanding will grow without end as we pass through the mansion worlds, the local universe, and the superuniverse until we reach Paradise. The fact that we do not fully understand God now is no reason for our faith to waver. Rather, it is a promise that eternal learning and discovery await us. Paper 106 says that the infinity of God should be the supreme assurance of our endless growth (see Paper 106, section 7).

The passage then states a very important fact: unqualified infinity is meaningless to the finite creature, but infinity is capable of self-limitation and is susceptible of reality expression to all levels of universe existences. The infinite God humbles himself to reveal himself in ways we can receive. He indwells us as the Thought Adjuster, takes on flesh like ours as a Creator Son, and abides beside us as the Spirit of Truth. The Infinite is not a distant abstraction but One who limits himself in order to draw near to us.

And the passage concludes: the face which the Infinite turns toward all universe personalities is the face of a Father, the Universal Father of love. This truth, that the face the deepest and highest reality in the universe shows us is the face of love, is a comfort beyond all philosophical speculation. Though we cannot fathom infinity, we know that the face with which infinity looks upon us is love. That alone is enough for us to come to him in confidence.

Today, if your heart has been heavy because of the things about God you cannot understand, lay that burden down. What we cannot know now, eternity will slowly make known to us. Our task now is to look upon the face the Infinite has turned toward us, the face of the loving Father, and to draw near to him as his children. When you pray, picture that warm face in your heart. Though we do not fully know him, we can rest in his arms. Just as a child finds peace in his father’s embrace without understanding everything about him, we too can find rest in the love of the infinite Father. Understanding will grow through eternity, but the fact that we are beloved children is already ours now.
d205.pr: Before you pray, remember that the infinite God is turning toward you the face of a loving Father.

d206.t: The Gift of the Time Lag
msg: The sixth section of Paper 105 describes the various repercussions in the universe when finite reality came into being. Among them, today’s passage deals with how divinity responds to the imperfection inherent in the time lag of evolution. In the universe there are things that are perfect from the beginning and things that are being perfected in time. Havona and Paradise are perfect, but the evolutionary universes in which we live are completed little by little over long ages. This slowness, this time lag, often feels to us like a painful limitation.

The passage says that the divinity response to this imperfection is disclosed in the compensating presence of God the Sevenfold. God the Sevenfold is the sevenfold association of Deity, beginning with the Paradise Trinity and reaching out through the Seven Master Spirits to the Creator Sons, that comes near to the creatures of time and space. Through his activities that which is perfecting is integrated with both the perfect and the perfected. God does not abandon the evolutionary universes to time alone; he is present in the very midst of their imperfect process, compensating for it.

The passage says that this time lag is inseparable from evolution, which is creativity in time. And it adds an astonishing fact: this time lag makes possible creature participation in divine creation by permitting creature personalities to become partners with Deity in the attainment of maximum development. If everything had been complete from the beginning, there would have been nothing for us to do. But because it takes time, we can enjoy the delight of making something together with God.

The passage shows how close this partnership is: even the material mind of the mortal creature thus becomes partner with the divine Adjuster in the dualization of the immortal soul. Our soul is made neither by the Adjuster alone nor by us alone. Our choices and the Adjuster’s leading are woven together, and a soul that will survive forever grows (see Paper 111, section 3). Our day-to-day decisions are actually being used to shape something eternal.

This teaching lets us see our slowness and immaturity with entirely different eyes. We are often disappointed with our own slow growth, impatient with the shortcomings of others, and frustrated that the world improves so slowly. But that slowness is not failure; it is an opportunity to participate. God the Sevenfold also provides techniques of compensation for the experiential limitations of inherent perfection as well as for the preascension limitations of imperfection. Our shortcomings have already been taken into account in God’s plan.

Today, when faced with your own slowness or that of others, choose patience instead of impatience. The very place that is not yet finished is the place where you can work together with God. One small good decision you make today is part of shaping your soul together with the Adjuster, and one piece added to the Supreme Being’s becoming actual in the evolving universe. Time is not a burden but a gift. Because the painting is not yet finished, we too can take up the brush. God delights not so much in showing us a finished painting as in painting it together with us. So do not be ashamed of an unfinished today; add one stroke of love to it.
d206.pr: When you grow impatient with your own slowness or someone else’s, think of it instead as an opportunity to work together with God.

msg: Paper 106 is a majestic and profound paper dealing with the various levels of universe reality and the integration of Deity that will unfold in future universe ages. It speaks of the experiential Trinities and the Trinity of Trinities, and it shows us horizons of distant eternity that the finite mind can hardly imagine. Its seventh section deals with the finality of destiny, and there the paper says that however deeply we come to understand the Father, our minds will always be staggered before his infinity (see Paper 106, section 7). Today’s passage tells us what attitude we should have before that very fact.

The passage is clear from its first words: such inability to attain God in a final sense should in no manner discourage universe creatures. We can never fully fathom or contain the infinity of God. But this is neither failure nor defeat. The passage says that we can and do attain Deity levels of the Sevenfold, the Supreme, and the Ultimate. And it says that these mean to us what the infinite realization of God the Father means to the Eternal Son and to the Conjoint Actor in their absolute status of eternity existence.

These words are truly astonishing. They mean that the God we can attain is a God who is more than enough for us. Just as the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit enjoy full satisfaction in the Father, so ascending mortals will enjoy full satisfaction and fulfillment at the levels of Deity they can attain. We are not meeting a God who is somehow lacking, a half God. We are meeting the whole God, who reveals himself in a way perfectly suited to our level of existence.

The passage then turns our perspective completely around. Far from harassing the creature, the infinity of God should be the supreme assurance that throughout all endless futurity an ascending personality will have before him the possibilities of personality development and Deity association. If God were finite, someone who could one day be fully known, our growth too would one day come to an end. But because God is infinite, there is no end to our growth, our discovery, and our love. These possibilities even eternity will neither exhaust nor terminate.

This truth gives deep meaning to our daily lives as well. We often want to stop with the thought, “I know enough; this is enough.” Or, on the contrary, we fall into the helplessness of thinking that no matter how hard we try, we can never reach God. The passage urges us to move beyond both. We should be humble because we do not fully know God, and yet hopeful because we can come to know him more each day. The endless God promises an endless adventure.

Today, let us begin with a heart ready to learn one new thing about God. In a verse of scripture, a scene in nature, or an encounter with another person, discover some new aspect of the Father. And rejoice that this discovery is never the last. Before us lies an eternally inexhaustible God, an eternally unending path of growth. That God is infinite means that for us new mornings will go on forever. Today’s insight becomes a stepping-stone to a greater insight tomorrow, and that path never comes to a dead end. In the endless God, our growth too is without end.
d207.pr: Write down one new thing you came to understand about God today, and give thanks for the endless path of learning.

msg: The last section of Paper 106 deals with the highest of philosophical themes, existential infinite unification. After its deep discussion of the Trinity of Trinities and the I AM, the paper comes down, surprisingly, to a very practical conclusion. At the end of all that majestic cosmology, what remains for us is a life lived doing the will of God. Today’s passage holds this very conclusion, and it shows in condensed form the core teaching that runs through the whole of The Urantia Book.

The passage speaks of a truth that sooner or later all universe personalities begin to realize: the final quest of eternity is the endless exploration of infinity, the never-ending voyage of discovery into the absoluteness of the First Source and Center. It says that all creature growth is proportional to Father identification, and that living the will of God is the eternal passport to the endless possibility of infinity itself. How far we can go into eternity depends not on the amount of our knowledge but on how much we have come to resemble the Father.

The passage says that in this universe age the realities of the Father are revealed within the qualities of divinity, and that these qualities are personally appropriated in the experience of living divinely. And it adds that to live divinely means actually to live the will of God. Becoming like God does not mean acquiring mysterious powers; it means living out divine qualities such as love, mercy, and sincerity in everyday life. The eternal voyage toward infinity begins with one ordinary choice I make today.

The following paragraph paints a concrete picture of such a life. To material, evolutionary, finite creatures, a life predicated on the living of the Father’s will leads directly to the attainment of spirit supremacy in the personality arena and brings such creatures one step nearer the comprehension of the Father-Infinite. Such a Father life is one predicated on truth, sensitive to beauty, and dominated by goodness. Truth, beauty, and goodness, these three supreme values, are the pillars of the life of one who lives the will of God.

The passage also shows the inner and outer life of such a person. Such a God-knowing person is inwardly illuminated by worship and outwardly devoted to the wholehearted service of the universal brotherhood of all personalities, a service ministry filled with mercy and motivated by love. Worship and service are the two wings of a God-knowing life. And all these life qualities are unified in the evolving personality on ever-ascending levels of cosmic wisdom, self-realization, God-finding, and Father worship. As Paper 111 says, to choose the Father’s will is the spiritual finding of the spirit Father (see Paper 111, section 5).

Today, let us practice taking this eternal passport into our hands. It need not be anything grand. Speak the truth, recognize beauty, and do one good deed. In the morning and evening worship the Father for a moment, and during the day serve one brother in love. As days of living God’s will accumulate in this way, we go a little deeper into the endless exploration of infinity. That the highest truth of the universe and our most ordinary day are joined together in this way is the greatest comfort this paper offers us. A small day lived in the will of God is one step on the eternal journey toward infinity.
d208.pr: Today, consciously speak one truth, seek out one beauty, and do one good deed.

msg: Paper 107 deals with the origin and nature of Thought Adjusters. It begins by saying that although the Universal Father dwells personally on Paradise, at the center of all things, he is at the same time actually present in the minds of countless mortals in innumerable universes. The means by which he does this is the Thought Adjuster. Today’s passage portrays this wondrous gift in several beautiful phrases: the Adjusters are the actuality of the Father’s love incarnate in the souls of men; they are the veritable promise of man’s eternal career imprisoned within the mortal mind.

First, consider the phrase the actuality of the Father’s love. We often hear that God loves us, but that love can sometimes feel distant and vague. Yet the passage says that this love has actually come to dwell within us. The Father does not merely love us from afar; he has sent a fragment of himself to live within us. The indwelling of the Adjuster is the surest proof that God’s love is not an idea but a reality.

The passage also says that the Adjuster is the essence of man’s perfected finaliter personality, which he can foretaste in time. The Adjuster helps man progressively master the divine technique of achieving the living of the Father’s will, and accompanies him step by step through the ascension of universe upon universe until he actually attains the divine presence of his Paradise Father. The seed of what we will one day become is already within us. The Adjuster is that seed and, at the same time, the gardener who makes it grow.

The following paragraph explains why God came as the Adjuster. God, having commanded man to be perfect, even as he is perfect, has descended as the Adjuster to become man’s experiential partner in the achievement of that supernal destiny. God is not one who merely lays down an impossible demand and watches from afar. Along with the call to be perfect, he gives both the power and the companion to fulfill that call. This is the fairness and the mercy of the Father.

The passage says that the fragment of God which indwells the mind of man is the absolute and unqualified assurance that man can find the Universal Father in association with this divine Adjuster. And its last sentence is deeply moving: the Adjuster came forth from God to find man and sonship him even in the days of the flesh. Before we sought God, God first came seeking us. And he makes us his sons and daughters not after we have become perfect, but already now, in these days of frail flesh.

Today, let us recall many times that the Father’s love has actually come to dwell within us. When loneliness sweeps over you, when you feel insignificant, when the call to be perfect feels too heavy, quietly turn your heart inward. There dwells the spirit of the Father who came seeking you and made you his child. Simply knowing this gives us the strength to rise again. The Father is far above in heaven and at the same time in the deepest place of our thoughts. His love has not merely been told to us in words; it has actually come to live within us. Whoever remembers this day by day knows, in any trial, that he has not been forsaken. And that knowing gives us the courage to walk once more toward perfection.
d209.pr: Three times today, pause for a moment to remember that the Father’s love has actually come to dwell within you, and give thanks.

msg: The fourth section of Paper 107 deals with the nature and presence of the Adjusters. It explains that to call the Adjuster divine is to recognize the nature of its origin, and it says that no Adjuster has ever been disloyal to the Paradise Father. At the end of all this explanation comes today’s passage. It is less an explanation than an earnest question put to us: Can you really realize the true significance of the Adjuster’s indwelling?

The author of the passage seems to feel that we pass over this fact far too easily. He asks again: Do you really fathom what it means to have an absolute fragment of the absolute and infinite Deity, the Universal Father, indwelling and fusing with your finite mortal natures? We often hear this truth once, nod our heads, and go back to our daily lives. But it is one of the most astonishing facts in the universe. An actual fragment of the One who made all things is within me right now.

The passage tells what this fact means for our destiny: when mortal man fuses with an actual fragment of the existential Cause of the total cosmos, no limit can ever be placed upon the destiny of such an unprecedented and unimaginable partnership. Our future is not confined by our frail nature. Because the One within us is infinite, our future as we become one with him is also without end.

The passage says that in eternity man will be discovering two infinities. One is the infinity of the objective Deity; the other is the unending potentiality of the subjective fragment of this same God, the Adjuster within us. We will not only discover God outwardly as we explore the universe, but also endlessly discover the God within as we journey inward. Always will the Adjuster be revealing to the mortal personality the wonder of God, and never can this supernal revelation come to an end, for the Adjuster is of God and as God to mortal man.

This truth changes the way we look at ourselves and at others. If a fragment of God dwells within me, I am never insignificant. And if a fragment of the same Father dwells within the people around me, they too deserve deep respect. Paper 110 says that the Adjuster dwells within the earthly tabernacle of our body and mind (see Paper 110, section 1). Our body, mind, and very life are a holy place where God abides.

Today, carry this question in your heart: Do I really realize the God who is within me? When you look in the mirror, when you look into another person’s face, remember the spirit of the Father who dwells there. And sit quietly for a moment and listen inwardly. In that stillness the Adjuster will reveal to us, little by little, the wonder of God. The more we come to realize this truth, the more reverent and the more joyful our lives become: reverent because a holy One dwells within us, and joyful because the future we share with him has no end. Realizing the fragment of God within us is the most beautiful discovery, one that will continue all our lives, indeed forever. Take one step in that discovery today.
d210.pr: Remember that the spirit of the Father dwells in the people you meet today, and show one of them a deeper respect.

d211.t: The Adjuster Turns Fear to Love
msg: Paper 108 deals with the mission and ministry of Thought Adjusters. Its fifth section explains what the Adjuster actually does within our minds, and the paper says that the Adjuster is not merely a thought helper but a thought adjuster (see Paper 108, section 5). The Adjuster works with our material mind, building up within it a spiritual counterpart. Today’s passage takes up the part of that work that touches our lives most urgently: changing fear into love and confidence.

The passage says that the Thought Adjusters would like to change our feelings of fear to convictions of love and confidence. The Father’s spirit within us does not want us to live in the grip of fear. But the passage immediately adds an important fact: they cannot mechanically and arbitrarily do such things; that is our task. Because God respects our free will, he does not force upon us changes to which we have not consented.

What, then, are we to do? The passage gives a very concrete picture. In executing those decisions which deliver us from the fetters of fear, we literally supply the psychic fulcrum on which the Adjuster may subsequently apply a spiritual lever of uplifting and advancing illumination. A lever can exert its force only when it has a fulcrum. When our small decision becomes the fulcrum, the great power of the Adjuster goes to work upon it.

This picture gives us great courage. We do not have to overcome all our fears by ourselves. We need only make one small decision not to be ruled by fear: deciding to make the phone call we dread, to begin the conversation we have put off, to pray instead of worrying, to take a step instead of doubting. That decision may look small, but the spirit of God works upon it. Our part is to set the fulcrum in place; the lifting is done by the Adjuster.

The following paragraph offers another comfort. When it comes to the sharp and well-defined conflicts between the higher and lower tendencies of the races, between what really is right or wrong, we can depend upon it that the Adjuster will always participate in some definite and active manner in such experiences. The fact that such Adjuster activity may be unconscious to us does not in the least detract from its value and reality. When we struggle before temptation, we are never fighting alone. Unseen but surely, the Father’s spirit stands on our side and fights with us.

Today, let us find one fear that binds us. Then make and carry out a small decision that takes one step away from that fear. Trust that in that moment the Adjuster is using your decision as a fulcrum to lift you up. As Paper 113 says, even the angels find it hard to understand why we are so dominated by fear (see Paper 113, section 2). Fear is not where we truly belong. Love and confidence are the home in which the Father’s children are meant to live. The way to overcome fear is not some grand heroic act but a succession of small decisions. If we set one fulcrum today, tomorrow we can set another from a little higher ground. Lifted up one step at a time in this way, our hearts move out of the prison of fear into the wide fields of love and confidence.
d211.pr: Name one fear that is holding you today, and carry out one small decision that frees you from it.

msg: The last section of Paper 108 bears the title God in Man. It says that the Adjuster is the wellspring of spiritual attainment and the hope of divine character, and that while we are human parents, the Adjuster is truly our divine parent (see Paper 108, section 6). The Adjuster is also the faithful custodian of our future career, making spirit duplicates of all our mental creations. Today’s passage concludes this section and the whole paper by lifting our gaze toward the eternal future.

The passage first tells us what we have begun: we humans have begun an endless unfolding of an almost infinite panorama. It is a limitless expanding of never-ending, ever-widening spheres of opportunity for exhilarating service, matchless adventure, sublime uncertainty, and boundless attainment. We are not beings who live once and then vanish. We are pilgrims who have already taken the first step of an eternal journey.

The phrase sublime uncertainty stands out here. Uncertainty usually breeds anxiety. Yet the passage calls it sublime. If everything were fixed in advance and fully known, there would be no adventure and no growth. Because there are things we do not yet know, there is the joy of discovery; because there are things we have not yet achieved, there is the reward of attainment. Paper 111 says that uncertainty in time together with security in eternity is the very essence of the Paradise adventure (see Paper 111, section 7).

But the passage also knows that on this journey there are days when clouds gather: times when hardship comes, when we cannot see the way ahead, when hope grows dim. The passage says plainly what our faith must do at such times: when the clouds gather overhead, our faith should accept the fact of the presence of the indwelling Adjuster. Whatever the circumstances, the fact that God is within us does not change. That fact becomes our anchor in the storm.

And that faith lifts our eyes to look farther. The passage says that we should be able to look beyond the mists of mortal uncertainty into the clear shining of the sun of eternal righteousness on the beckoning heights of the mansion worlds of Satania. Clouds can hide the sun, but they cannot destroy it. When an airplane climbs through the clouds, the sun is always shining above them. Faith is the eye that sees above the clouds. Even if all is dark before us now, the sun is still shining.

Today, if clouds are covering you, do not fix your gaze on them. Instead, remember the presence of the Adjuster within you and look to the eternal sun shining beyond. Your present difficulty is only one scene in an endlessly unfolding panorama. Beyond that scene, exhilarating service and matchless adventure await us. Our faith shines brighter when circumstances are dark than when they are bright. The thicker the clouds, the clearer grows the eye that looks to the sun beyond them, and the deeper our trust in the Father’s spirit within us. The mists of this world will one day lift, and in the morning of the mansion worlds we will see that sun face to face. Look toward that day, and endure today, and rejoice.
d212.pr: If clouds are covering your heart today, picture the eternal sun shining beyond them and offer a short prayer.

msg: Paper 109 deals with the relation of Thought Adjusters to universe creatures. It says that Adjusters are the children of universe career, and that virgin Adjusters, when first dispatched, are beings who must accumulate experience. The first section explains the development of Adjusters, and today’s passage states the principle of that development in a single sentence: actual living experience has no cosmic substitute. This short sentence is a deep law running through the entire universe.

The passage tells us something astonishing: the perfection of the divinity of a newly formed Thought Adjuster does not in any manner endow this Mystery Monitor with experienced ministrative ability. As a fragment of God the Adjuster is perfect in nature, but experience can be gained only by actually living. If even a fragment of God cannot skip experience, we mortals can hardly hope to mature without it. Experience is inseparable from a living existence.

The passage defines experience this way: it is the one thing which no amount of divine endowment can absolve us from the necessity of securing by actual living. God gives us many things freely. Life, personality, the Adjuster, the Spirit of Truth are all gifts. But experience alone cannot be given as a gift. It becomes ours only when we live it ourselves. However good the books we read, we learn to swim only by getting into the water, and we learn to love only by actually loving.

The passage goes on to say that, in common with all beings living and functioning within the present sphere of the Supreme, Thought Adjusters must acquire experience; they must evolve from the lower, inexperienced, to the higher, more experienced, groups. This journey from virgin Adjuster to advanced Adjuster and on to supreme Adjuster runs parallel to our own. The Adjuster gains experience by living with us, within us. As Paper 110 says, the Adjusters are interested in our daily affairs and in the many details of our lives (see Paper 110, section 1).

This teaching gives new meaning to every moment of our lives. The joys and sorrows, successes and failures, meetings and partings we go through are all experience that we and the Adjuster are building up together. Neither dull routine nor painful trials are in vain. They are a precious treasure that can be gained in no other way. This teaching also lets us lay down the temptation to look for shortcuts. There is no magic secret to spiritual maturity. There is only the path of living faithfully day by day.

Today, let us receive the things before us not as burdens we would like to avoid but as opportunities for irreplaceable experience. There is something to learn even in a difficult conversation, an unfamiliar task, or the repetition of daily routine. And remember that in every one of those moments the Adjuster within you is also learning and growing. We are eternal partners who live together and mature together. Experience does not accumulate overnight, but it accumulates without missing a single day. A day I have lived faithfully today becomes a treasure that no knowledge or gift can replace, engraved in my soul and added to the Adjuster’s experience as well. So do not make light of today’s ordinariness. It is the surest school of preparation for eternity.
d213.pr: Choose one task you would rather avoid today, and do it as an opportunity for irreplaceable experience.

msg: The sixth section of Paper 109 deals with the persistence of true values. It tells of the Adjuster’s triumph in the life of Jesus and of the work that Adjuster now does in the local universe (see Paper 109, section 6). And at its very beginning stands today’s passage, which opens with some of the most comforting sentences in all of The Urantia Book: Adjusters never fail; nothing worth surviving is ever lost.

The passage widens this principle: every meaningful value in every will creature is certain of survival, irrespective of the survival or nonsurvival of the meaning-discovering or evaluating personality. The true meanings we have grasped in life, the love we have practiced, the truth we have held, the beauty we have recognized never vanish into thin air. They are preserved forever in the universe. This is a promise that God never discards anything of worth.

The passage goes further and says that this principle holds even in the saddest case. A mortal creature may reject survival; still the life experience is not wasted. The eternal Adjuster carries the worth-while features of such an apparent life of failure over into some other world and there bestows these surviving meanings and values upon some higher type of mortal mind, one of survival capacity. Even if one person’s life ends in tragedy, the good things that were in it go on living in the life of another.

And the passage concludes: no worth-while experience ever happens in vain; no true meaning or real value ever perishes. These words give deep meaning to the hidden labors of our lives. Kindness no one noticed, effort that bore no fruit, sincerity no one understood, tears of prayer shed in secret: none of these are ever in vain. Paper 108 says that nothing entrusted to the Adjuster is ever lost, and that it keeps every true value safe for our eternal future (see Paper 108, section 5).

This teaching lifts up hearts that have sunk into disappointment and futility. Sometimes we ask, What was the use of everything I did? There are times when our devotion to our children goes unrewarded, when living honestly seems to bring only loss, when loving seems to leave only wounds. But the passage tells us that if there was true value in it, it has never disappeared. Visible results may vanish, but the eternal values we have built up are kept safe in God’s hands.

Today, let us recall one past labor that felt futile. Then look for the love, truth, and goodness that were in it. They have not disappeared. And today, plant one more such value. It is all right if you do not see the result. For the Adjuster never fails, and nothing of worth is ever lost. Our task is not to control results but to plant values. We can leave the harvest to God. Even if we never see the fruit in this world, the true values we have planted will surely blossom in eternity. Those who hold this faith do not lose heart; they can quietly go on doing good today as well.
d214.pr: Recall one past labor that seemed to end without fruit, find the true value in it, and give thanks to God.

msg: Paper 110 deals with the relation of Thought Adjusters to individual mortals. Its first section explains that the Adjuster does not live in the material brain but indwells the mind, and says that the Adjuster is interested not only in our spiritual preparation but in our daily affairs and the many details of our lives (see Paper 110, section 1). Today’s passage shows how closely and how patiently this indwelling spirit stays with us, and where that relationship is heading.

The passage first says that the Adjuster remains with us in all disaster and through every sickness which does not wholly destroy the mentality. When we are ill, when we have failed, when it seems we have lost everything, the Father’s spirit does not leave us. Even when people walk away and circumstances collapse, the companion within remains to the end. This is the most faithful companionship we can ever know.

But the passage goes on to remind us of our responsibility. How unkind knowingly to defile or otherwise deliberately to pollute the physical body, which must serve as the earthly tabernacle of this marvelous gift from God. All physical poisons greatly retard the efforts of the Adjuster to exalt the material mind. And the passage mentions poisons of the mind as well: the mental poisons of fear, anger, envy, jealousy, suspicion, and intolerance likewise tremendously interfere with the spiritual progress of the evolving soul.

This list becomes a very practical checklist for us. We try hard to avoid what harms the body, but we are less careful about what harms the mind. Yet long-nursed anger, envy born of constant comparison, and suspicion and intolerance toward others sicken our souls just as poisons sicken the body. Keeping clean the house in which the Adjuster dwells means caring for the mind as well as caring for the body. A forgiving, grateful, and trusting heart keeps that house pure.

The following paragraph shows the beautiful destination toward which all this is heading: today we are passing through the period of the courtship of our Adjuster. Courtship is a time of getting to know one another, of bringing hearts into harmony, of preparing for the day of becoming one. If we only prove faithful to the trust reposed in us by the divine spirit who seeks our mind and soul in eternal union, there will eventually ensue that morontia oneness, that supernal harmony, that celestial fusion. That union, the passage says, is so perfect and final that even the most experienced personalities can never recognize the mortal and the Adjuster as separate identities.

Let us live today as a day of courtship with the Adjuster. As we take care of ourselves for the sake of someone we love, keep your body and mind pure for the sake of the holy companion within you. Find one poison of the mind and lay it down, and fill its place with trust and gratitude. The more faithful we are, the nearer our oneness with him comes, and one day we will be beings eternally one with him. The time of courtship need not be hurried, but neither should it be neglected. Opening our hearts to him each day, if only briefly, and making one by one the choices that would please him, is how we continue this holy courtship. Even on the days we stumble, the Adjuster does not leave in disappointment but waits patiently. Answer that faithful waiting today with a small act of faithfulness. That is the surest step toward eternal union.
d215.pr: Find one poison in your heart today, whether fear, anger, envy, or suspicion, and change it into gratitude and trust.

msg: The third section of Paper 110 deals with co-operation with the Adjuster. It says that the Adjusters are playing the sacred and superb game of the ages, engaged in one of the supreme adventures of the universe (see Paper 110, section 3). The success of the Adjuster in guiding us through this mortal life depends greatly on our co-operation. Today’s passage, in a voice of regret, points to a common habit of ours that stands in the way of such co-operation.

The author of the passage says: “⟦Q 110:3.4⟧I cannot but observe that so many of you spend so much time and thought on mere trifles of living, while you almost wholly overlook the more essential realities of everlasting import.⟦/Q⟧” Those essential realities are the accomplishments concerned with the development of a more harmonious working agreement between us and our Adjusters. We spend our days with our hearts caught up in what to wear, how others see us, small losses and gains. Meanwhile the things that will truly last forever are pushed aside.

The passage makes clear the true goal of our lives: the great goal of human existence is to attune to the divinity of the indwelling Adjuster; the great achievement of mortal life is the attainment of a true and understanding consecration to the eternal aims of the divine spirit who waits and works within our minds. The word attune is beautiful. As an instrument is tuned to pitch, tuning our minds to the note of the Adjuster is the greatest work of life.

But here the passage strikes a very important balance: a devoted and determined effort to realize eternal destiny is wholly compatible with a lighthearted and joyous life and with a successful and honorable career on earth. Living a spiritual life does not mean turning our backs on the world and losing our laughter. Co-operation with the Thought Adjuster does not entail self-torture, mock piety, or hypocritical and ostentatious self-abasement. The idea that tormenting and degrading ourselves is holiness is a misunderstanding.

The last sentence of the passage sums it all up: the ideal life is one of loving service rather than an existence of fearful apprehension. We need not live in anxious fear that we may fail to please God. Rather, living with a joyful heart, loving and serving people, is the best way to co-operate with the Adjuster. Jesus, too, was not a man of sorrows but a soul of gladness (see Paper 100, section 7).

Today, let us look at where our time and thoughts are going. Take part of the time you spend on trivial worries, comparisons, and complaints, and turn it into time for quietly attuning your heart to the Father. Then, with a heart so attuned, serve people joyfully. Eternal things are accomplished not in heaviness and gloom but in light and joyful loving service. Trifles in themselves are not bad. The ordinary tasks of eating, working, and caring for a home are precious too. The trouble comes when they take up the whole of our hearts and crowd out what is eternal. Those who keep attunement with the Adjuster at the center of their hearts even while doing little things can fill ordinary days with eternal meaning. On the faces of those who live this way, peace dwells instead of worry, and joy instead of heaviness.
d216.pr: Take ten minutes you would have spent on small worries today, and use them to quietly attune your heart to the Father.

msg: Paper 111 deals with the relation between the Adjuster and the soul. Its first section says that mind is the arena of choice. The Adjuster’s work is spiritual, but it must be carried out upon our intellectual mind. The paragraph just before says that man does not passively and slavishly surrender his will to the Adjuster but chooses actively, positively, and co-operatively to follow the Adjuster’s leading (see Paper 111, section 1). Today’s passage shows this relationship in a picture anyone can easily understand.

The picture is this: mind is your ship, the Adjuster is your pilot, the human will is captain. The ship is the vessel in which we travel. The pilot knows the sea, the stars, and the course, and guides the way to the destination. And the captain is the one who holds final authority over the ship. The most important thing in this picture is that the captain is ourselves. The Adjuster knows the way, but he does not seize the helm. The decision is always ours.

The passage says that the master of the mortal vessel should have the wisdom to trust the divine pilot to guide the ascending soul into the morontia harbors of eternal survival. A wise captain listens to a pilot who knows the sea better than he does. When storms rage and fog hides the way ahead, if the captain insists on his own stubborn way, the ship is in danger. But a captain who trusts his pilot can cross any sea.

The passage also speaks honestly of shipwreck. Only by selfishness, slothfulness, and sinfulness can the will of man reject the guidance of such a loving pilot and eventually wreck the mortal career upon the evil shoals of rejected mercy and upon the rocks of embraced sin. Here we see three dangers: the selfishness that thinks only of itself, the slothfulness that puts off what must be done, and the sinfulness that knowingly chooses wrong. These three drown out the voice of the pilot.

But the passage ends in hope. With our consent, this faithful pilot will safely carry us across the barriers of time and the handicaps of space to the very source of the divine mind and on beyond, even to the Paradise Father of Adjusters. The key word is consent. The Adjuster is always ready. All that is needed is for us, the captain, to consent willingly to the pilot’s guidance.

Today, let us look at where the ship of our life is heading. Are we listening to the pilot’s voice, or turning the helm by our own stubborn will? Before an important decision, pause for a moment and quietly ask which direction the pilot within you is pointing. And if that direction leads toward more love, more honesty, and more service, then as captain gladly turn the helm that way. The voyage does not end in a day. We need to correct the helm every day and every day consent anew to the pilot’s guidance. Sometimes we turn the helm the wrong way. But each time the faithful pilot shows us the right course again. What matters is not never making a mistake but, after a mistake, trusting the pilot again and turning the helm. When we do this, our ship will surely reach the Father’s harbor.
d217.pr: Before one decision you make today, pause to ask which direction the pilot within you is pointing, and follow it.

msg: The fifth section of Paper 111 deals with the consecration of choice. It tells us that doing the will of God is nothing more or less than an exhibition of creature willingness to share the inner life with God (see Paper 111, section 5). And it adds that such a choice is not a surrender of will but a consecration of will, an expansion of will, and a glorification of will. Today's passage unfolds this teaching more deeply, showing what choosing the Father's will is and where it leads.

The passage first tells us that this choosing of the Father's will is the spiritual finding of the spirit Father by mortal man, even though an age must pass before the creature son may actually stand in the factual presence of God on Paradise. We have not yet seen God with our eyes. Yet in the very moment we choose his will, we have already found him spiritually. The surest way to find God is to do his will.

Then the passage draws a very delicate distinction. This choosing does not so much consist in the negation of creature will, “⟦Q 111:5.6⟧Not my will but yours be done,⟦/Q⟧” as it consists in the creature's positive affirmation: “⟦Q 111:5.6⟧It is my will that your will be done.⟦/Q⟧” The difference looks small, but it is immense. The first can sound like the voice of a will suppressed and resigned. The second is a glad declaration of a will that freely desires the Father's will. God is not looking for servants who submit under compulsion but for children who gladly will with him.

The passage also shows us where this choice leads. If this choice is made, sooner or later will the God-choosing son find inner union, fusion, with the indwelling God fragment. And this same perfecting son will find supreme personality satisfaction in the worship communion of the personality of man and the personality of his Maker. The deepest satisfaction we seek lies not in possessions or achievements but in personal fellowship with God.

The last sentence of the passage is truly beautiful. The creative attributes of these two personalities have eternally joined in self-willed mutuality of expression, and this is the birth of another eternal partnership of the will of man and the will of God. Choosing the will of God does not mean that I disappear; it means that God and I are joined as eternal partners. My individuality is not erased; rather, it blossoms most fully in union with God.

Today, when you pray, confess this affirmation from the heart: Father, it is my will that your will be done. Say it not grudgingly but gladly, not in resignation but in trust. Then, throughout the day, recall that confession at every small moment of choice. As those choices accumulate, we find the Father and grow into eternal partnership with him. At first this confession may not come easily. There will be times when my wishes and the Father's will seem to pull in different directions. But the more we trust that the Father's will always aims at our true good, the more this confession becomes sincere. And one day we will discover that desiring the Father's will is no longer forced but has become our own most natural longing. That is the freedom the consecration of will brings.
d218.pr: This morning and this evening, gladly confess, “⟦Q 111:5.6⟧It is my will that your will be done.⟦/Q⟧”

d219.t: The Power and Responsibility of Choice
msg: Paper 112 deals with personality survival. It tells us that personality is a potentially eternal gift bestowed by the Universal Father upon his creatures, and that it is absolutely unique in time, space, and eternity (see Paper 112, the introduction and section 1). The fifth section explains the survival of the human self, and today's passage reveals the key that decides that survival: the very power of choice, the universe insignia of freewill creaturehood.

The passage says that this power of choice constitutes man's greatest opportunity and his supreme cosmic responsibility. Opportunity and responsibility are two sides of the same coin. That we can choose means that our choices truly matter. If all our actions were determined in advance, we would bear no responsibility, but neither would we grow. By giving us the freedom to choose, God has established us as true personalities and as his co-workers.

The passage then sets out a series of astonishing facts. Upon the integrity of the human volition depends the eternal destiny of the future finaliter. Upon the sincerity of the mortal free will the divine Adjuster depends for eternal personality. Upon the faithfulness of mortal choice the Universal Father depends for the realization of a new ascending son. And upon the steadfastness and wisdom of decision-actions the Supreme Being depends for the actuality of experiential evolution. The high beings of the universe are leaning on our small choices.

Reading these sentences slowly, the heart overflows. The infinite Universal Father awaits our faithful choices. The Adjuster within us can attain eternal personality only through our sincere decisions. And even the evolving Supreme Being becomes actual through our wise decisions. We are never insignificant spectators of the universe. Each of our choices genuinely contributes to the shaping of eternal reality.

This truth gives new weight to our everyday decisions. Whether to be honest or to lie, to forgive or to resent, to serve or to turn away: these small choices are never small. Yet this should not plunge us into fear. God does not demand that we be perfect; he wants us to be sincere and faithful. As Paper 103 tells us, the Father deals with us not according to our actual virtue but according to our motives and intentions.

Today, let us live conscious of the choices we make. Each time you stand before a decision, remember that this is a choice that shapes something eternal. And choose the way of integrity, sincerity, faithfulness, and wisdom. When we choose this way, the Adjuster rejoices, the Father gains a new son or daughter, and the universe comes a little closer to completion. Choice is not over in a single moment; it is given to us anew every day. Even if we chose wrongly yesterday, we can choose rightly again today. Paper 112 tells us that every will creature will surely have a real opportunity to make one undoubted, true, and final choice (see Paper 112, section 5). So do not be bound by past failures; give your whole heart to the choices set before you today. God is always waiting with hope for our next choice. It is ours to answer that waiting with faithfulness.
d219.pr: Before one small choice today, remember that it is a decision that shapes eternity, and choose the most faithful way.

msg: The final section of Paper 112 deals with Adjuster fusion. It tells us that fusion imparts eternal actuality to personality, and that through fusion the Universal Father fulfills his promise to give himself to his creatures (see Paper 112, section 7). It also tells us that fused mortals, after entering the Corps of the Finality and reaching Paradise, will take up new service in the future universes of outer space. Today's passage opens with an exclamation of wonder before this majestic future.

The passage cries out: What an adventure! What a romance! And it pictures the substance of that adventure: a gigantic creation to be administered by these personalized and humanized Adjusters, these Adjusterized and eternalized mortals, these mysterious combinations and eternal associations of the highest known manifestation of the essence of the First Source and Center and the lowest form of intelligent life capable of comprehending and attaining the Universal Father. This picture of the highest and the lowest become one in the service of the universe is truly wondrous.

The passage says that such amalgamated beings, such partnerships of Creator and creature, will become superb rulers, matchless administrators, and understanding and sympathetic directors of all forms of intelligent life that may come into existence in the future universes of the outer space levels. Why mortals, of all beings? Because only those who have started at the very bottom and climbed through every stage themselves can truly understand and sympathize with creatures struggling in the lowly places. Our experience of weakness and struggle will become our most precious asset for serving others in the future.

The next paragraph honestly acknowledges our reality: True it is, you mortals are of earthly, animal origin; your frame is indeed dust. The Urantia Book does not glamorize human origins. We have come up from the animal through a long process of evolution, and we still live with the limitations of that inheritance. But the passage does not stop there. It declares that the door of eternity stands open to this being made of dust.

The passage says: if you actually will, if you really desire, surely the heritage of the ages is yours, and you shall someday serve throughout the universes in your true characters, children of the Supreme God of experience and divine sons of the Paradise Father of all personalities. The key here is willing and desiring. It is not our origin but our will that determines our destiny. Though we began in the dust, if only we desire it, we can become sons and daughters of God serving among the stars.

Today, if your weaknesses and limitations discourage you, remember this passage. Our bodies are dust, but within us dwells the Father's spirit, and before us lies an eternal adventure. And once more, from the depths of your heart, desire it: Father, I truly want to be your son, your daughter. That sincere desire is the first step on the path that runs from dust to the stars. This adventure is not only a matter of the distant future. It has already begun, right here, where we desire and choose the Father's will today. We are already living the first chapter of that wondrous romance. We live our days in bodies made of dust, yet within those days we are growing as eternal sons and daughters.
d220.pr: When you feel your weakness, remember that an eternal adventure has been promised even to you, a being of dust, and resolve anew.

msg: Paper 113 deals with the seraphic guardians of destiny, the beings we commonly call guardian angels. It plainly states that the teaching about guardian angels is not a myth but a fact (see Paper 113, section 1). The second section explains how the guardians of destiny are assigned and how they serve, and today's passage lets us hear the hearts of the angels: how they feel toward us and what grieves them. This passage helps us sense the angels not as distant, mysterious beings but as warm and close friends.

The passage first tells us that the angels develop an abiding affection for their human associates. And it adds that if we could only visualize the seraphim, we would develop a warm affection for them. Guardian angels are not sentries guarding us out of duty. They are companions who cherish and love us. They volunteered to take charge of us, and they serve at our side until our lives are over. Even while we do not know them, they know and love us deeply.

The passage also says that, divested of material bodies and given spirit forms, we would be very near the angels in many attributes of personality. The angels share most of our emotions and experience some additional ones we do not yet know. So they understand most of our joys and sorrows, our hopes and discouragements. It is a great comfort to know that beings who rejoice when we laugh and grieve when we weep are always beside us.

Yet the passage says there is one emotion the angels find difficult to comprehend. It is the legacy of animal fear that bulks so large in the mental life of the average inhabitant of Urantia. The angels really find it hard to understand why we so persistently allow our higher intellectual powers, even our religious faith, to be so dominated by fear, so thoroughly demoralized by the thoughtless panic of dread and anxiety. These words are less a rebuke than the sorrow of one who loves.

This passage holds up a searching mirror. We live swayed by fear far more than we realize. Worry about tomorrow, anxiety over what others think of us, dread of failure and loss: these steer our decisions. And that fear paralyzes even our intellect and our faith. We say we believe in God and yet tremble with anxiety; we know what is right and yet fail to do it out of fear. Fear is merely a legacy inherited from our animal origins, not a burden the children of God must carry to the end. Paper 108 tells us that the Adjuster longs to change our fears into the convictions of love and confidence (see Paper 108, section 5).

Today, each time fear rushes in, think of the guardian angel at your side. That angel wonders why you are so afraid and longs earnestly for you to trust the Father more. Then give your fear a name. Say: this is only the legacy of animal fear; I am a child of God. The Father's spirit dwells within us, and a loving angel stands beside us. For one who remembers this, fear can no longer be master.
d221.pr: Each time fear rises, name it as only the legacy of animal fear, and trust the Father.

d222.t: The Angels Who Guard Our Freedom
msg: The fifth section of Paper 113 deals with seraphic ministry to mortals. Guardian angels help and guide us at countless moments of our lives, but their help has clear boundaries. Today's passage shows both what those boundaries are and how deeply the angels care for us within them. It beautifully reveals the one principle that all of God's spiritual helps hold in common: respect for the free will of man.

The passage first names what the angels do not do. Angels do not invade the sanctity of the human mind; they do not manipulate the will of mortals; neither do they directly contact the indwelling Adjusters. The human mind is a holy sanctuary. It is the place where a person meets the Father's spirit within, and even the angels do not enter it lightly. The guardian of destiny influences us in every possible manner consistent with the dignity of our personality, but under no circumstances does it interfere with the free action of the human will.

The passage broadens this principle further: neither angels nor any other order of universe personality have power or authority to curtail or abridge the prerogatives of human choosing. This is an astonishing fact. The mighty beings of the universe stop short before our choices. So precious and so holy is the free will God has given to man. Paper 111 tells us that the captain of the ship of the mind is the human will (see Paper 111, section 1). Neither angel nor Adjuster takes the helm from us.

This does not mean the angels are indifferent. The next paragraph tells us that angels are so near us and care so feelingly for us that they figuratively “⟦Q 113:5.2⟧weep because of your willful intolerance and stubbornness.⟦/Q⟧” Seraphim do not shed physical tears; they have no physical bodies, nor do they possess wings. But they do have spiritual emotions, and they experience feelings and sentiments of a spiritual nature which are in certain ways comparable to human emotions. When we take a wrong road, they do not stop us by force, but they grieve deeply.

This passage shows us the true face of love. True love does not manipulate the other. It respects freedom and yet stays near to the end; it does not coerce even before a wrong choice, but grieves and waits instead. This is the way God loves us, and the way the angels love us. And it is also the way we ought to love others. If we claim to love a child, a spouse, or a friend while taking away their freedom and trying to move them according to our will, we are far from the love of angels.

Today, let us remember two things. First, my choices are wholly my own, and so they are precious and carry responsibility. I must not use carelessly the freedom that even the angels respect. Second, approach the people you love as an angel would. Do not coerce, do not manipulate, but respect their freedom and stay by their side. And if there is an angel grieving over my stubbornness, let me lay down one piece of that stubbornness today and gladden that angel.
d222.pr: Today, respect the choices of someone you love, staying beside them instead of pressing them, and lay down one piece of your own stubbornness.
